Definition: properly, the inner bark of the papyrus plant, i.e. (by implication) a sheet or scroll of writing:--book.
BiblicalUsage: The book is the written record, and the word opens the New Testament itself: the book of the generation of Jesus Christ, in Matthew 1:1. Luke 3:4 quotes the book of the words of Isaiah, Philippians 4:3 says the fellow-labourers' names are in the book of life, and Revelation 20:15 warns that whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the book of life is the record that decides everything, and I hold that my name is there because Christ wrote it, not because I earned it.
